title: Analytics indexes are duplicated by raw SQL migration
reasoning: The initial Event model already creates indexes on (event_type, -timestamp) and (content_type, object_id, -timestamp). Migration 0005 then creates raw SQL indexes on the same column sets, producing duplicate indexes with different names. This increases migration time, storage, and write overhead for every Event insert/update without adding a new access path.
recommendation: Remove the redundant RunSQL operations or replace them with state-aware Django AddIndex operations only if the existing indexes are intentionally being renamed. If the migration has already shipped, add a follow-up migration to drop the duplicate raw SQL indexes safely.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or migration checks are included that inspect generated database indexes or detect duplicate equivalent indexes.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a schema/migration test that introspects indexes on events_event after migrations and asserts there is only one index for each intended analytics column set.
minimumFixScope: Delete or replace the duplicate index creation in 0005 and, if needed, add a cleanup migration for installations that already applied it.
